chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Abī al-Miʿzā, from Samāʿah, from ʿAlī, who said:
I asked al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام about the junub and the menstruating woman: may they dye themselves? He said: There is no harm.

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ الصَّالِحَ: a title referring to the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.يَخْتَضِبَانِ: they two apply dye, such as henna

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a junub person or a menstruating woman to use dye?
ai.summary: This hadith states that there is no problem with a person in janabah or a menstruating woman using dye. It conveys a jurisprudential ruling indicating the permissibility of this act despite the state of ritual impurity.
